Build only this feature on this page. Get it working, test it, and then move on.

What you are building

Turn the modal form into a working create flow that stores a new record and refreshes the list.

The key idea for this feature is POST requests and record insertion.. Before you write anything, make sure you can describe what the user should see or what the request should do when this feature is finished.

Key words and definitions

TermMeaning
POST requestA request used to create a new record.
PayloadThe data sent with the request.
InsertAdding a new record to storage.
RefreshUpdating the interface so the new record is visible.

Why the client needs this

  • The system must let staff create tasks reliably, not just see an empty interface.
  • This feature turns the modal from a layout into a working client action.

Bring this forward from earlier pages

  • Check the schema before you write the payload so the names match the stored fields.
  • Use your validation notes to decide which checks happen in HTML, JavaScript, and Flask.

POST request terms

  • request.get_json() reads the JSON body Flask received.
  • Content-Type: application/json tells the server how to interpret the body.
  • After a create action, the UI should prove success by reloading the list.

Create flow outcome

The important moment is not the click. It is the new record appearing back in the list after storage succeeds.

Save task Writes to SQL
New task now visible in the list

How this feature moves through the stack

HTMLJavaScriptFlaskStorageResponse

Useful reference before you code

  • A create flow starts in the form, passes through the backend, and ends with refreshed evidence on screen.
  • Front-end validation improves usability, but back-end validation still matters.
  • The class should be able to trace where every submitted value goes.

Generic create-request pattern

const payload = { title, priority };

fetch("/api/items", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
  },
  body: JSON.stringify(payload)
}).then(() => loadItems());
payload

This is the JavaScript object you want to send to the backend.

method: "POST"

POST is the HTTP method commonly used when creating a new record.

Content-Type

This header tells the server the request body contains JSON.

JSON.stringify

Turns the JavaScript object into JSON text for the request body.

Build it in this order

A create feature is a chain: read values, package them, send them, store them, then redraw evidence on screen.

Step 1 static/js/app.js

Read the current form values

  • Use the control ids you created earlier to read the latest modal values.
  • Store those values in clearly named variables before building the request.
Step 2 static/js/app.js

Build the payload and send the POST request

  • Create one JavaScript object that holds the submitted values.
  • Send it as JSON with the correct HTTP method and headers.
  • After the request succeeds, refresh the task list so the user sees evidence.
Step 3 app.py

Receive the JSON and insert the new record

  • Read the request body in Flask.
  • Validate the values again because the browser cannot be trusted on its own.
  • Insert the new record into storage and return a clear success response.

Ask yourself

  • Why do the backend checks still matter if the form already had `required`?
  • How will you know whether the problem is in the payload or the insert?

Where the checks happen

HTML

The interface can require fields, constrain control types, and guide the user before submit.

JavaScript

The browser can check presence, shape, and request timing before sending data.

Flask

The backend must re-check the request because outside tools can bypass the browser entirely.

SQL / SQLite

Database rules keep the stored record sensible and consistent.

Where your work goes

File or areaWhy this file mattersWhat belongs in this feature
templates/index.htmlCaptures the input valuesConfirm field names match the data meaning
static/js/app.jsSends the create requestRead form values and submit structured data
app.pyReceives and validates create requestsPersist the new record safely

When this feature is ready to sign off

  • The form submits structured data.
  • Required fields are checked before submission.
  • The new task appears after a successful create action.
